reachable: No at the scored position; yes in training. At the scored read the router is structurally disconnected: the instrument's layout has odd L and the wrapper returns the unwrapped output before route_chain is ever called, so gradient from the scored prediction reaches zero of the 18 router parameters (guard_reach: n_inert = 18, i.e. all of them). In training the mechanism does get gradient, from two directions: the aux InfoNCE/MSE on `reads` (which the ramp turns on over 300 steps and which mines real supervision — the max_dup=3 filter does exclude the content-free mv steps on this data), and the main objective flowing back through `contrib` into out_scale and the keys. So the candidate is not dead weight — but everything it can contribute to comp_ca must travel indirectly, through whatever the aux's pred_weight=0.5 InfoNCE term does to the TRUNK, minus whatever the train/eval `contrib` skew costs. The hypothesis's own causal story ("changes M, which changes V, which changes what the read returns") is inoperative at scoring.
solves_outside_model: Clean — no outside-the-model resolution. The head never sees text: route_chain consumes only tok_emb, the same frozen 768-d embeddings the trunk gets, and every key, gate and mixing coefficient is a learned linear/GELU function of them. It parses no command, indexes no path, and holds no lookup table. The aux's use of observation duplicates (dup_o / dup_c, computed under torch.no_grad) is sample SELECTION and contrastive-target choice at train time only — aux_loss is called solely from evolve/harness._train — which is explicitly permitted. Causality is intact by construction where the code runs: a_src and the routing matrix M are strictly lower-triangular (allow requires pos_i > pos_j), U0 at position i is read only by positions after i, and live_obs only zeroes a step's own content contribution, so reads_i depends on {c_1..c_i} and {obs_1..obs_{i-1}}. I verified padding safety by execution: a fully-padded row and position 0 both read exactly 0.0 with no NaN (the null column works as described). Nothing here resembles the retracted stream that stamped a resolved answer into a token.
summary:
The mechanism this hypothesis is named for does not run at scoring time. The cups instrument builds its scored window as [cmd_0, obs_0, ..., cmd_r] — length 2r+1, ODD, because the read's observation is truncated rather than padded. The head gates its entire routing contribution on `2 * (L // 2) == L`, so on every scored forward it returns the trunk's output untouched. I confirmed this three ways: by reading build_cups_layout, by executing the real wrapped net at L=13 and L=14 (diff 0.0000 vs 2.2440), and by running the reachability gate, which reports exactly 18 inert parameters — the complete _ClosureRouter. Both comp_ca arms use that same odd tensor, so the router contributes zero to native_hit and zero to swap_stayed. The hypothesis's two central sections, "WHY THIS SHOULD MOVE comp_ca" and "THE EVAL-TIME GATE, EXPLICITLY", are therefore false as implemented — and the second is ironic: the author reasoned carefully about the withheld observation being "padded, zeroed, or truncated" and concluded the read would be unchanged, without noticing that truncation flips the sequence parity his own guard keys on.

Worse than inert, it is asymmetric. At training L is even (60 on the fixture), the wrapper fires, and the main objective puts gradient on all 18 router parameters including out_scale (max|grad| 1.3e-3 at step 1). So out_scale drifts off zero, the trunk is trained against pred + contrib, and then is scored on pred alone. The candidate as written is a train-time auxiliary plus an unintended train/eval offset — not a path-addressed content store read at the scored position.

Everything else in the proposal is honest and checks out. The Neumann-series algebra is exactly as claimed: I reran the author's own 6-step board with ideal keys and the final read is X with the two intermediate move reads also X. The null column, the causal masking and the padding behavior all do what the text says. The crossover is described accurately (parent's arch/optim/target/batcher-with-identical-params/stream, partner's objective), and the claim that both parents' r18 head is dead is true — no arch in evolve/chunks/arch defines transition_from_emb. The mining rule's max_dup=3 does separate contentful steps from the 8-15-member constant-observation clusters on the real jail data, and the specific step-14/step-22 duplicate the author cites is genuine. One stated measurement is wrong: appends are 7.0% of steps (51/724) or 20.2% of mutating ops, not "~40% of the ops" — and that number is the sole justification for the 2-simplex mixing coefficients.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: how far out_scale actually drifts under the real 
step budget, so I cannot size the train/eval skew — it could be negligible or it could dominate; whether the aux's pred_weight InfoNCE on the trunk helps or hurts comp_ca on its own; the mining yield on the real training root (I only had the 24-sequence jail sample); and any actual score, since I ran no training.

divergences.claim: "This router's read at the scored position is A_src[scored, :] V ... So native_hit rises and swap_stayed falls, which is the differential." And the whole section THE EVAL-TIME GATE, EXPLICITLY: "The scored position is a command whose own observation is withheld. Nothing in the read path is gated on that observation ... if the harness pads, zeroes, or truncates the final observation, the read at the scored command is unchanged."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The routing contribution is a structural no-op at every scored forward pass. cups_probe.build_cups_layout builds Lmax = 2 * max(w['r']) + 1 — an ODD length: the read's observation is not padded, it is absent, so the tensor is [cmd_0, obs_0, ..., cmd_r]. The head's wrapper computes n = L // 2 and returns the unwrapped output whenever 2*n != L, which is true for every odd L. route_chain has the identical guard. Both comp_ca arms (cups_probe.measure with ctx['tok'], cups_probe.alt_chain with cache['tok2'], a clone of the same tensor) go through _fwd_pred on that odd layout, so the router contributes exactly zero to native_hit AND to swap_stayed. The author anticipated padding and zeroing of the final observation; the instrument does neither — it truncates, which changes the sequence PARITY, and parity is the one thing the head is gated on.
divergences.evidence: evolve/cups_probe.py:109 `Lmax = 2 * max(w["r"] for w in wins) + 1`. head__r5_closure_routing_memory.py:212-215 `L = tok_emb.size(1); n = L // 2; if n < 2 or 2 * n != L: return out`; same guard at :131-133. EXECUTED: built the real genome's arch, wrapped it, set out_scale=1.0 and perturbed the router; max|wrapped - unwrapped| = 2.2440 at L=14 and 0.0000 at L=13. EXECUTED: eval/guard_reach.analyze on the candidate genome returns n_params 130, n_inert 18, n_dead 0 — the 18 inert parameters are exactly the 18 _ClosureRouter parameters (src_in.w/b, dst_in.w/b, path_key.w, ctl_in.w/b, move_gate.w/b, read_gate.w/b, mix_coef.w/b, log_temp, log_decay, null_src, null_dst, out_scale). The gate passes only because an aux-only head is exempt from the inert check.

divergences.claim: Implicit throughout: the router's additive read is the model's prediction path, and the aux "keeps the read in the raw observation scale it is being added in" — i.e. the contribution the trunk is trained alongside is the contribution that is scored.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Creates an unclaimed and adverse train/eval skew. At training the stream's collate produces an EVEN L (2*maxn), so the wrapper is fully live: it adds `contrib` to the trunk's prediction, and the main objective's gradient flows into all 18 router parameters including out_scale. So out_scale moves off its zero init and the trunk learns to produce a `pred` that is correct only after `contrib` is added. At scoring `contrib` is identically zero. The net is therefore evaluated with a term it was trained to depend on removed. This is not a neutral no-op: it is a systematic offset between the training and scoring prediction, whose size grows with however far out_scale drifts.
divergences.evidence: EXECUTED on the guard_reach fixture with the real genome: stream.collate gives L = 60 (even), the wrapper fires, and after backward on the MAIN objective alone (no aux term) all 18/18 router parameters carry nonzero gradient, with max|grad| on out_scale = 1.296e-3 at step 1. evolve/harness.py:70-73 wraps before make_opt(net.parameters()), so out_scale is optimized. Contrast with the L=13 result above where contrib is exactly 0.

divergences.claim: "Those append steps are ~40% of the ops in this data, and the r2 prior's single source read cannot express them at all" — the stated justification for the 2-simplex mixing coefficients (a, b).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The number is wrong by roughly 2-6x depending on what 'ops' means, and the mechanism it justifies is in the dead path anyway. Counted over all 24 jail sequences: 724 steps total, of which 51 contain '>>' (7.0% of steps). Restricting to mutating ops (mv 172 + '>>' 51 + '>' 30 = 253), appends are 20.2%. Neither reading is ~40%. The author had the file and could have counted; this is a stated measurement that does not hold.
divergences.evidence: EXECUTED over evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: verb tally cat 365, mv 172, ls 106, APPEND('>>') 51, REDIR('>') 30. 51/724 = 0.0704; 51/253 = 0.202.
